tooltip.title: CTCL Workup by Test Type
tooltip.markdown: The diagnostic evaluation for CTCL integrates tests from multiple modalities, from routine blood work to advanced molecular and imaging studies.

tooltip.title: Basic Laboratory Studies
tooltip.markdown: These initial blood tests establish the patient's baseline health, assess overall disease burden, and identify key prognostic markers.

tooltip.title: Complete Blood Count with Differential
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** Quantifies white blood cells, lymphocytes, and eosinophils. The absolute lymphocyte count is essential for calculating the absolute Sézary cell count.
-   **Relevance:** Can reveal lymphocytosis or eosinophilia, common findings in advanced CTCL.

tooltip.title: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** Assesses baseline liver (ALT, AST, bilirubin) and kidney (creatinine) function.
-   **Relevance:** Critical before starting systemic therapies, many of which can be hepatotoxic or require dose adjustment for renal impairment.

tooltip.title: Lactate Dehydrogenase
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** A non-specific marker of cell turnover.
-   **Relevance:** Elevated LDH is an independent adverse prognostic factor in advanced MF/SS, indicating higher tumor burden and potentially large-cell transformation.

tooltip.title: Flow Cytometry (Peripheral Blood)
tooltip.markdown: The primary method for quantifying blood involvement (B stage) and diagnosing Sézary Syndrome.

tooltip.title: CD4:CD8 Ratio
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** Measures the ratio of helper (CD4+) to cytotoxic (CD8+) T-cells.
-   **Relevance:** A ratio >10 is one criterion for B2 blood involvement.

tooltip.title: Loss of Pan-T-Cell Antigens
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** Malignant T-cells often lose expression of normal T-cell markers.
-   **Relevance:** Loss of CD7 or CD26 on a significant portion of the CD4+ population is a key diagnostic criterion for Sézary Syndrome. (e.g., >40% CD4+CD7- cells).

tooltip.title: Absolute Sézary Cell Count
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** To directly quantify the tumor burden in the blood.
-   **Relevance:** An absolute count ≥1000 cells/μL is a major criterion for diagnosing Sézary Syndrome and defines B2 blood involvement.

tooltip.title: Pathology Tests
tooltip.markdown: Direct examination of tissue is essential for diagnosis and staging.

tooltip.title: Skin Biopsy (Histopathology)
tooltip.markdown: The single most important diagnostic test. Shows atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism.

tooltip.title: TCR Gene Rearrangement (Clonality)
tooltip.markdown: Identifies a dominant T-cell clone in skin or blood, supporting a diagnosis of lymphoma.

tooltip.title: Lymph Node Biopsy
tooltip.markdown: Required for staging if palpable lymphadenopathy is present.
